newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on interest rate concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on interest rate concerns.

text.p: Thai stocks ended down in thin trade on Friday on investor concerns about high Thai interest rates used by the government to boost the baht, traders said.

The SET Index lost 1.38 points, or 0.18 percent, to 747.76. The SET 50 fell 0.16 points, or 0.29 percent, to 54.73. Turnover fell to a modest 1.50 billion baht partly due to closure of regional markets to mark the Lunar New Year, traders said.
"Very little happened in the market today. The volumes were very low and people were looking at the money market," said an trader at TISCO.

Remarks by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Friday that Thai interest rates would have to remain high to defend the baht helped push the market down by over one percent in the afternoon before late buying pared losses, traders said.
Tight liquidity in the interbank market also triggered concern with the overnight rate rising to a six-month high of 25-28 percent in the afternoon.
"The market has seen money flowing out of equities, not just today but all through the week," said one trader.
Delta Electronics closed at its daily 10 percent limit high after it was oversold earlier, analysts said. The maker of power switching supplies and monitor components ended up seven baht at 77.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, losing one baht at 174, Banpu shed 16 to 428, and Advanced Info rallied eight to 238.
